name: Sikaflex-400 Fire

SIKAFLEX®-400 FIRE: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikaflex®-400 Fire, April 2023, Version 02.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/8/sikaflex_-400_fire.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikaflex®-400 Fire where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.03).
1.2 Product description. Sikaflex®-400 Fire is a fire resistant, polyurethane, 1- part, moisture-curing, elastic joint sealant. Movement capability ±35 %. Internal and external use.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikaflex®-400 Fire is designed for fire rated movement and connection joints and penetrations on porous and non-porous substrates.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikaflex®-400 Fire
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Fire resistant polyurethane joint sealant
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - ASTM C920-14 Class 35, Sikaflex®-400 Fire, MST, Report No 1117920V-SIKA
    - Fire Resistance AS 1530.4, Sikaflex®-400 Fire, CSIRO, Report No FSP 1819
    - Fire Resistance AS 1530.4, Sikaflex®-400 Fire, Exova, Report No 376610B
    - Fire Resistance AS 1530.4 Sikaflex®-400 Fire, CSIRO, Report No FSP 1839
    - Fire testing EN 13501-2, Sikaflex®-400 Fire, Exova, Report No 391651
    - Performance Test EN 15651-1, Sikaflex®-400 Fire, SKZ, Report No 123504/16-III
    - Test ISO 11600, Sikaflex®-400 Fire, SKZ, Report No 123504/16-IV
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS 1530.4: cited elsewhere in the data sheet; listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1); Characteristics / Advantages (p.1).
    - EN 1366-4: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Characteristics / Advantages (p.1).
    - ASTMC719: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Characteristics / Advantages (p.1).
    - ASTM C920-14: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 13501-2: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 15651-1: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - ISO 11600: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - ISO 1183-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.1).
    - ISO 8339: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Secant tensile modulus (p.1).
    - ISO 9047: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Movement capability (p.2).
    - ASTM C 719: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Movement capability (p.2).
    - ISO 7389: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Elastic recovery (p.2).
    - CQP 049-2: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Curing rate (p.2).
    - CQP 019-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Skinning time (p.2).
    - CQP 019-2: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Tooling time (p.2).
    - AS1530.4: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Further Information (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Up to 4 hours fire resistance according to AS 1530.4
    - Up to 4 hours fire resistance according to EN 1366-4
    - Movement capability ±35 % (ASTMC719)
    - Easy to smooth and good workability
    - Good adhesion to many different substrates
    - Long open time
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: 1- part Polyurethane
    - Colour: Grey
    - Density: ~1.40 kg/l (ISO 1183-1)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Secant tensile modulus: ~0.30 N/mm² at 100 % elongation (23 °C); ~0.45 N/mm² at 100 % elongation (−20 °C) (ISO 8339)
    - Tensile strain at break: ~650 % (ISO 37)
    - Movement capability: ±25 %; ±35 % (ISO 9047) (ASTM C 719)
    - Elastic recovery: ~85 % (ISO 7389)
    - Tear propagation resistance: ~5.0 N/mm (ISO 34)
    - Service temperature: −40 °C to + 70 °C
    - Resistance to fire: Refer to ‘Approvals / Certificates’, Sika Passive Fire Protection Handbook or contact Sika Technical Services for specific information.
    - Joint design: Refer to ‘Approvals / Certificates’, Sika Passive Fire Protection Handbook or contact Sika Technical Services for specific information.
2.7 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 600 ml foil pack (20 per box)
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production if, stored according to the storage conditions.
    - Storage conditions: The product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +35 °C. Always refer to packaging.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.03) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - The substrate must be sound, clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, cement laitance, old sealants and poorly bonded paint coatings which could affect adhesion of the sealant. The substrate must be of sufficient strength to resist the stresses induced by the sealant during movement.
    - Removal techniques such as wire brushing, grinding, grit blasting or other suitable mechanical tools can be used.
    - Repair all damaged joint edges with suitable Sika repair products.
    - New or refurbished joints must be saw-cut.
    - Where joints in substrate are saw cut. After sawing, all slurry material, must be flushed away and joint surfaces allowed to dry.
    - All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of any activators, primers or sealant.
    - Sikaflex®-400 Fire adheres without primers and/or activators.
    - For optimum adhesion, joint durability and critical, high performance applications such as joints on multistorey buildings, highly stressed joints, extreme weather exposure or water immersion / exposure. The following priming and/or pre-treatment procedures must be followed:
    - Non-porous substrates
    - Aluminium, anodised aluminium, stainless steel, PVC, galvanised steel, powder coated metals or glazed tiles. Slightly roughen surface with a fine abrasive pad. Clean and pre-treat using Sika® Aktivator-205 applied with a clean cloth.
    - Before sealing, allow a waiting time of > 15 minutes (< 6 hours).
    - Other metals, such as copper, brass and titanium-zinc, cleaned and pre-treat using Sika® Aktivator-205 applied with a clean cloth. After a waiting time of > 15 minutes (< 6 hours). Apply Sika® Primer-3 N applied by brush. Before sealing, allow a waiting time of > 30 minutes (< 8 hours)
    - Porous substrates
    - Concrete, aerated concrete and cement based renders, mortars and bricks surfaces must be primed using Sika® Primer-3 N or Sika® Primer-210 applied by brush.
    - Before sealing, allow a waiting time of > 30 minutes (< 8 hours).
    - For more details such as application and flash-off times, refer to the most recent Product Data Sheet of the respective pre-treatment product.
    - Adhesion tests on project specific substrates must be performed and procedures agreed with all parties before full project application.
    - Contact Sika Technical Services for additional information.
    - Note: Primers and activators are adhesion promoters and not an alternative to improve poor preparation / cleaning of the joint surface. Primers also improve the long term adhesion performance of the sealed joint.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Sag flow: ~0 mm (20 mm profile, 50 °C) (SO 7390)
    - Backing material: Refer to ‘Approvals / Certificates’, Sika Passive Fire Protection Handbook or contact Sika Technical Services for specific information.
    - Curing rate: ~2.5 mm/24 hours (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 049-2)
    - Skinning time: ~180 minutes (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
    - Tooling time: ~150 minutes (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 019-2)
4.3 Consumption.
    | Joint width | Joint depth | Joint length |
    | mm | mm | m per foil pack (600 ml) |
    | 10 | 10 | 6 |
    | 15 | 10 | 4 |
    | 20 | 10 | 3 |
    | 25 | 12 | 2 |
    | 30 | 15 | 1,3 |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.4 Mixing. 1-part ready to use
4.5 Application method / tools.
    - Reference must be made to further documentation where applicable, such as relevant method statement, application manual and installation or working instructions.
    - Masking
    - It is recommended to use masking tape where neat or exact joint lines are required. Remove the tape within the skin time after finishing.
4.6 Application method / tools - Joint Backing.
    - After the required substrate preparation, insert a suitable backing rod to the required depth.
    - Priming
    - If required, prime the joint surfaces as recommended in substrate preparation. Avoid excessive application of primer to avoid causing puddles at the base of the joint.
    - Application
    - Sikaflex®-400 Fire is supplied ready to use.
    - Prepare the end of the foil pack or cartridge, insert into the sealant gun and fit the nozzle. Extrude Sikaflex®-400 Fire into the joint ensuring that it comes into full contact with the sides of the joint and avoiding any air entrapment.
    - Finishing
    - As soon as possible after application, sealant must be firmly tooled against the joint sides to ensure adequate adhesion and a smooth finish.
    - Use a compatible tooling agent (e.g. Sika® Tooling Agent N) to smooth the joint surface. Water can be used. Do not use tooling products containing solvents.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Sika® Remover-208 immediately after use. Hardened material can only be removed mechanically.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Sikaflex®-400 Fire can be over-painted with most conventional facade paint coating systems. However, paints must first be tested to ensure compatibility by carrying out preliminary trials (e.g. according to ISO technical paper: Paintability and Paint Compatibility of Sealants). Optimum results are obtained when the sealant is allowed to fully cure first. Note: non-flexible paint systems may impair the elasticity of the sealant and lead to cracking of the paint coating. Depending on type of paint used, plasticizer migration may occur causing the paint to become surface ‘tacky’.
    - Colour variations may occur due to the exposure in service to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV-radiation. This effect is aesthetic and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
    - Do not use on natural stone.
    - Do not use on bituminous substrates, natural rubber, EPDM rubber or on any building materials which might leach oils, plasticisers or solvents that could degrade the sealant.
    - Do not use to seal joints in and around swimming pools.
    - Do not use for joints under water pressure or permanent water immersion.
    - Do not expose uncured Sikaflex®-400 Fire to alcohol containing products as this may interfere with the curing reaction
4.9 Further information.
    - Safety Data Sheet (SDS)
    - AS1530.4 test report
    - Sika passive fire protection handbook
    - Pre-treatment Sealing and Bonding Chart

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C to +40 °C
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5 °C to +40 °C. Minimum 3 °C above dew point temperature
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Colour variations may occur due to the exposure in service to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV-radiation. This effect is aesthetic and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: ~1.40 kg/l (ISO 1183-1)
    - Secant tensile modulus: ~0.30 N/mm² at 100 % elongation (23 °C); ~0.45 N/mm² at 100 % elongation (−20 °C) (ISO 8339)
    - Tensile strain at break: ~650 % (ISO 37)
    - Movement capability: ±25 %; ±35 % (ISO 9047) (ASTM C 719)
    - Elastic recovery: ~85 % (ISO 7389)
    - Tear propagation resistance: ~5.0 N/mm (ISO 34)
    - Sag flow: ~0 mm (20 mm profile, 50 °C) (SO 7390)
    - Curing rate: ~2.5 mm/24 hours (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 049-2)
    - Skinning time: ~180 minutes (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
    - Tooling time: ~150 minutes (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 019-2)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikaflex®-400 Fire, April 2023, Version 02.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/8/sikaflex_-400_fire.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikaflex 400 Fire, version 06/08/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/h/MSDS%20Sikaflex-400%20Fire%20GHS7.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
